name: Centro Historico
tagline: Pink cantera stone, the cathedral and the aqueduct
description: Morelia's UNESCO-listed core, built almost entirely from pink volcanic cantera, running from the cathedral along Madero to the aqueduct with its 253 arches. Colonial mansions now hold hotels, cafes and the university buildings. It is coherent, walkable and among the most handsome city centres in Mexico.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the cathedral, the aqueduct and the plazas on foot
pros: The cathedral, the aqueduct and the plazas within minutes
Cafes, restaurants and the sweet market close by
The most beautiful streets in the city
cons: The highest rents in the city
Thick colonial walls interfere with wifi indoors
Traffic and noise on the through streets

name: Chapultepec and Santa Maria
tagline: The leafy residential districts south of the aqueduct
description: The established residential neighbourhoods running south and east from the aqueduct, with tree-lined avenues, the Bosque Cuauhtemoc park, good restaurants and comfortable houses. It is the pleasant middle-class part of Morelia, ten minutes from the centre and considerably quieter.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a quiet neighbourhood near the centre
pros: Tree-lined streets and the city park
Ten minutes on foot or a short ride to the centre
cons: Requires a ride for the historic core

name: Ciudad Universitaria
tagline: Around the Michoacana university, students and cheap rents
description: The district around the Universidad Michoacana campus west of the centre, with student housing, cheap fondas, bookshops and a young population. Rents here are the lowest close to the centre, and the university's cultural programme and the film festival venues are nearby.
bestFor: Budget stays with the student social world close by
pros: The lowest rents near the centre
cons: Fifteen minutes from the historic centre

name: Altozano and the Northern Districts
tagline: The modern side, malls and newer apartments
description: The newer residential development north and northeast of the centre, with modern apartment complexes, gated communities, the malls and the supermarkets. It is where Morelia's professional families have moved and where the newest housing and best parking are, at moderate rents.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a modern flat, parking and everyday shopping
cons: Twenty minutes from the historic centre
Gated-community living is not for everyone

name: Patzcuaro (60 km southwest)
tagline: The Purepecha lake town, and the Day of the Dead
description: A colonial town on Lake Patzcuaro an hour southwest, at the heart of Purepecha country, with a whitewashed plaza, craft villages around the lake and the Day of the Dead observances on Janitzio island that are among the most significant in Mexico. It is smaller, cooler and cheaper than Morelia.
bestFor: Stays that want the lake and Purepecha country rather than a city
pros: Lake Patzcuaro and the craft villages around it
One of the great Day of the Dead observances
cons: An hour from Morelia and its services
Extremely busy around the start of November
